Title: Diagnosis
Details:
The failing test `testEncodingInputStreamAutodetect` checks if the encoding passed when creating archive input streams is respected. It does so by iterating through test cases, opening streams via `getInputStreamFor`, and comparing the expected encoding with the encoding retrieved from the created stream.

The method `getInputStreamFor` in `ArchiveStreamFactoryTest` calls the `ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream(InputStream)` method to get the archive input stream, without specifying an encoding argument.

Looking at the `ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream(InputStream)` method, the code tries to autodetect the archive type from the input stream's signature, then creates the appropriate archive input stream instance. Noticeably, for certain archive types like `ArjArchiveInputStream`, `DumpArchiveInputStream`, and others, the constructor called does not always use the `entryEncoding` field; some constructors are called without passing the encoding.

The other overloaded method `createArchiveInputStream(String archiverName, InputStream in)` accepts an archive name and input stream, and it correctly passes the `entryEncoding` when creating input streams for many archive types, including `ArjArchiveInputStream`, `CpioArchiveInputStream`, `DumpArchiveInputStream`, `JarArchiveInputStream`.

However, the autodetection method `createArchiveInputStream(InputStream)` does not consistently pass down the `entryEncoding` value for all archive input stream types. For example:
- `ArjArchiveInputStream` is created without passing the encoding.
- `DumpArchiveInputStream` is created regularly, though in the dedicated method it does pass `entryEncoding`.
- For `JarArchiveInputStream`, in the detection method it is only checked by its signature and not instantiated with the encoding; it only appears in the named version.

This discrepancy means that when archive streams are created by autodetection, the encoding field is not passed on for some archive types, causing the encoding to be lost and the tests expecting an encoding to fail.

The current bug report confirming "ArchiveStreamFactory fails to pass on the encoding when creating some streams (Arj, Cpio, Dump, Jar...)" matches this diagnosis.

Recent bug reports about immutability/thread safety and encoding defaults are somewhat related but do not contradict this diagnosis.

Hence, the root cause is that in the autodetection `createArchiveInputStream(InputStream)` method of `ArchiveStreamFactory`, the `entryEncoding` field is not passed to all archive input stream constructors that accept it.

The solution is to modify the autodetection method to pass the encoding for all relevant archive streams, ensuring the encoding passed to the factory is used in all created streams. This will satisfy the failing test that expects the encoding to be preserved.

---
